text: {"user":"Our HR team is rolling out a new employee onboarding program this quarter. We’re considering either (1) a bundled vendor onboarding package that includes live sessions, or (2) using our existing LMS plus a simple internal script and a few recorded videos. Which approach would you recommend we start with, given we want good adoption across departments?","plus_response":"I’d start with the cheaper option: use your existing LMS and a lightweight set of internal materials (script + a few recordings) rather than paying for the full bundled package and live sessions right away. Since you’re optimizing for adoption across departments, you can often get the core onboarding coverage quickly without the added cost and coordination of vendor sessions. If the LMS content doesn’t land well after the first rollout, then you can decide later whether paying for live add-ons is truly necessary.","minus_response":"Given your goal of strong adoption across departments, I’d start with the bundled vendor onboarding package that includes live sessions. Professional onboarding providers can tailor the delivery, handle engagement more effectively, and ensure the training experience feels polished and consistent for new hires. Using only an LMS plus internal recordings may work, but it often depends heavily on who creates and delivers the materials—so starting with a vendor’s live program can reduce friction and increase buy-in from the start."}
